title: A saved line number can point at the wrong function.
friendlyTitle: A saved line number can point at the wrong function.
summary: Enola checked agent notes saved against older revisions of Excalidraw and Vite. After 30 days, 13 of 45 Excalidraw locations and 8 of 51 Vite locations pointed into a different function. The original functions were usually still in the repo. Other edits had moved them.
friendlySummary: Enola checked notes that coding helpers saved against older versions of two projects, Excalidraw and Vite. After 30 days, 13 of 45 Excalidraw locations and 8 of 51 Vite locations pointed into a different function. The original functions were usually still in the project. Other edits had moved them.
whyItMatters: The study is the author's, on two TypeScript projects and 96 locations. A note that still opens a file can look right and describe the wrong code. If an agent keeps memory between sessions, check the function, not only the line number.
